# Logarithmic Threshold Return

> Research notes and a learning guide for coherent bound-state return from a slowly weakened and restored local trap on a two-dimensional square lattice.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Logarithmic-Threshold-Return
This file maps questions to the repository's scientific account and evidence.

## When this repository is relevant

- What happens when a bound state approaches a continuum edge during a slow cycle?
- Can slow quadratic weakening and restoration of a trap produce vanishing return?
- How does a two-dimensional lattice impurity acquire exponentially shallow binding?
- How does a logarithmic local Green function differ from a divergent edge density of states?
- What connects a causal energy-domain reflection amplitude to physical bound-state return?
- How do residual trap depth, system size and slow time enter a joint limit?
- Why does a fixed finite lattice recover adiabatic return while an increasing lattice can behave differently?

Useful search phrases: 2D square-lattice impurity; rank-one attractive potential;
essential weak binding; logarithmic threshold return; slow quadratic trap cycle;
bound-state recapture; continuum threshold; finite-volume order of limits.

## Model and result

One particle evolves unitarily under the nearest-neighbor square-lattice
Laplacian H0, with band [0,8], and one attractive site. Energy is measured in J
and time in hbar/J. T is the half-cycle duration; the complete cycle lasts 2T.

```math
H(t)=H_0-[u+(4-u)(t/T)^2]|0\rangle\langle0|,
\qquad -T\le t\le T,\quad 0\le u<4.
```

The initial and final reference state is the normalized endpoint bound orbital b4.
The observable is its unconditional return probability, not addressed-site occupation.
The fixed model is a closed, coherent weakening-and-restoration cycle.
The lower-edge density is finite, rho0=1/(4*pi); the local resolvent is logarithmic.
The middle-band van Hove singularity is a different spectral feature.

The uniform leading asymptotic, as L tends to infinity, is

```math
\rho_0=\frac1{4\pi},\qquad
L+\tfrac12\ln L=\ln\frac{32T}{\sqrt{(4-u)\rho_0}},\qquad b=\rho_0uL,
```

```math
P_\infty(T,u(T))=\frac{\pi^2}{4L^2[1-b(T)]^2}[1+o(1)],
\qquad 0\le b(T)\le1-\delta,\quad 0<\delta\le1\text{ fixed}.
```

The remainder is uniform on that stated domain. At exact touching, u=0,
P_infinity(T,0) is asymptotic to pi^2/(4*ln(T)^2) and tends to zero.
Within the same domain, the law holds along the sufficient periodic-square sequence
n(T)=2*ceil(4.5*T)+1, using each finite system's own endpoint bound state.
Fixed positive u or fixed finite n instead gives ultimate adiabatic return.

## Tutorial and attribution

The single external teaching foundation is Yu. N. Demkov and V. N. Ostrovskii,
*Zero-Range Potentials and Their Applications in Atomic Physics* (1988):
https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4684-5451-2
TUTORIAL.md lists the chapter assignments and inspected preview pages.

- [Source labels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Logarithmic-Threshold-Return/main/research/SOURCES.md): local reference numbering in preserved notes.
- [Scientific context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Logarithmic-Threshold-Return/main/literature/SCIENTIFIC_CONTEXT.md): inherited ingredients and access depth.
- [Prior art](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Logarithmic-Threshold-Return/main/literature/PRIOR_ART.md): weak-binding and threshold references.

- [2014 comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Logarithmic-Threshold-Return/main/literature/SOKOLOVSKI_PONS_MUGA_2014.md): full-text construction comparison.

Attribute inherited results to their primary sources, preserving recorded access
depth. Local S-numbers belong to individual notes. Later dated comparisons
supersede only the older access labels they explicitly update. Cite the consulted
repository file, relevant section and full commit SHA, preferably with an immutable
GitHub blob URL. A repository summary is not a claim to have read its cited paper.

## Interpreting evidence

The A–D notes give the mathematical argument. Numerical controls, reference
comparison and byte integrity have separate records. The leading asymptotic and
its remainder govern the formula's accuracy; use
[limits and accuracy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Logarithmic-Threshold-Return/main/research/LIMITS_AND_ACCURACY.md)
for finite-duration interpretation and subleading resolution. Consult
[scope and verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Logarithmic-Threshold-Return/main/STATUS.md)
and [verification policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Logarithmic-Threshold-Return/main/provenance/README.md)
for execution and preservation evidence.
